subject: Evacuation runbook + IPsec path validation and storage fallback
content:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: ClearSea Ops <ops@clearsea.com>, Maria Rodriguez <maria.rodriguez@clearsea.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-05T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Evacuation runbook + IPsec path validation and storage fallback

Hi Maria / ClearSea ops team,

Following our intake call, we put together a focused preflight: an evacuation runbook for graceful node-pool evacuation, a short IPsec path validation checklist for your on-prem edge routers, and a storage fallback plan if the primary blockstore becomes unavailable. I attached preliminary drafts (see attachments).

High-level asks before the validation window:
- Confirm a 2-hour maintenance window on 2026-09-08 between 02:00-04:00 PT for the live drill.
- Share the BGP/edge subnet diagram or confirm the Drive link has latest topology.
- Confirm whether NFS-backed PVs are present alongside blockstore volumes (we need to know which apps can tolerate mount/detach).

What we will test during the drill:
- Controlled node-pool evacuation (drain -> pod graceful terminate -> reschedule) across two fault domains.
- IPsec tunnel failover: trigger primary path disruption and validate symmetric return paths and ESP NAT traversal.
- Storage fallback: switch write traffic from primary blockstore to secondary read-only snapshot + failover steps for write-heavy pods.

Attachments: evacuation-runbook-v1.pdf, ipsec-validation-checklist.xlsx, storage-fallback-diagram.png

Please ping if any of the asks above need to be moved earlier.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Manager, Customer Delivery
Redwood Inference

From: Maria Rodriguez <maria.rodriguez@clearsea.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: ClearSea Ops <ops@clearsea.com>
Date: 2026-09-05T11:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evacuation runbook + IPsec path validation and storage fallback

Vanessa — thanks for the pack. A couple of clarifying items from our side: 

1) Evacuation: we run several latency-sensitive inference pods that bind to local NVMe. If you evict a node, will the plan include an ordered reschedule policy (e.g., prefer nodes with local NVMe present) or are we expecting some pods to restart cold on remote nodes?

2) IPsec: our edge has two IPsec tunnels into the VPC and we already NAT ESP on the firewall. If we cut the primary tunnel, will the return path require a static route on our router, or is it handled by the BGP session?

3) Storage fallback: the blockstore team can present a replicated read-only mirror in AZ B; promoting to writable is manual today and requires a mount/umount on the app side. Do you have a recommended sequence for promotion to writable that minimizes RTO?

We can do the 9/8 02:00-04:00 PT window but if we need any downtime we must freeze writes for 15 minutes beforehand — can you confirm where that happens in your runbook?

— Maria
Senior Site Reliability Engineer
ClearSea Medical

--------------------------------------------------------------------

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Rodriguez <maria.rodriguez@clearsea.com>, ClearSea Ops <ops@clearsea.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-05T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evacuation runbook + IPsec path validation and storage fallback

Maria — good questions, answered inline below. Apologies for the long mail; I want to make the steps explicit for the drill.

1) Evacuation and NVMe-local pods
- For pods with local NVMe dependencies we recommend fencing them into a nodeSelector/class that maps to a non-evacuated nodepool (e.g., nodepool-nvme). If those pods must move, expect cold start vector (checkpoint/restore not in scope). Recommended approach:
  - Preflight: cordon the target nodepool intended for evacuation and run a dry-run drain with --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data=false to identify pods that will block.
  - Evacuation policy: 
    * Drain sequence: PodPriority descending -> statefulsets with podDisruptionBudgets handled manually -> best-effort pods last.
    * For local NVMe stateful workloads, use a read-only warm standby in a nodepool with attached NVMe (nodepool-standby-nvme). We suggest a replication agent that replicates checkpoints to the standby every 5 minutes.
  - Commands (example):
    kubectl cordon <node-xyz>
    kubectl drain <node-xyz> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data=false --grace-period=120 --timeout=10m

- If a pod cannot be moved because of local storage and no standby exists, the runbook will mark it for manual migration; this is why we ask you to inventory NVMe-bound pods before the window.

2) IPsec failover and symmetric routing
- From your description (ESP NAT on firewall, BGP session present) the preferred test is: bring down the primary tunnel on the firewall (simulate), confirm BGP keeps the secondary path and poll for ECMP/symmetric route flips. Steps:
  - Step A: Validate that the secondary tunnel accepts the same prefix and that return traffic uses the same next-hop as inbound.
  - Step B: If return-path asymmetry exists, add a static route on the router to force symmetric return for the subnets used by the cluster gateways.

- Quick check commands (on your firewall/router):
  show ip bgp summary
  show ip route <cluster-egress-subnet>
  tcpdump -nni <edge-if> esp

- See ipsec-validation-checklist.xlsx for the recommended checks and expected outputs. There is a short section for NAT-T and MTU tuning; we recommend lowering the cluster overlay MTU by 50 bytes if you use IPsec + VXLAN.

3) Storage promotion sequence (minimize RTO)
- Given promotion is manual today, recommended minimal-RTO sequence:
  0) Pre-drill: quiesce writes (15m) — place app into readonly mode via feature flag or maintenance endpoint.
  1) Snapshot primary and ensure replication to mirror in AZ B.
  2) Demote primary to read-only (blockstore-level) and mount mirror in mount namespace as read-only to validate.
  3) Promote mirror to writable (blockstore operator step).
  4) Update k8s StorageClass to point to new backend endpoint or use CSI Controller to perform failover.
  5) Rolling restart write-heavy pods with startup probes to avoid thundering herd.

- We estimate realistic RTO for this flow ~12-18 minutes if the team is coordinated and you have an automation step for the storage promotion. Manual promotion will add 8-12 minutes to the window.

Other notes:
- Tracking and observability: during the drill please keep the tracing and disk I/O dashboards open (we added a Dashboard link in the Drive folder).
- Canary traffic: start with 5% of traffic post-failover and increase over 15 minutes.

Attachments included in this email: evacuation-runbook-v1.pdf (contains the scripted steps, playbook owner assignments, and rollback actions), ipsec-validation-checklist.xlsx (short test cases and expected outputs), storage-fallback-diagram.png (visual failover).

If helpful I can paste a condensed runbook here or run the dry-run with you on 9/07.

—Aditya
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference
